title: Fallback tokenizer + context + tooling compatibility upkeep
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Maintain the fallback variant compatibility matrix to ensure tokenizer behavior, context length handling, and tooling (function/tool-calling, structured outputs) remain compatible across primary and fallback model variants used by smart routing policies. Background: smart routing can route to lower-cost or regional variant models when primary capacity is constrained. Historically we have had subtle tokenizer and context-handling mismatches that cause truncation, token-count divergence, or tool-call schema drift when falling back. This ticket operationalizes a recurring maintenance sweep plus automation to detect and remediate incompatibilities before they hit production routes.
acceptance_criteria: Automated diff job runs daily and reports tokenizer tokenization mismatch rate between base and each fallback variant < 0.5% for our official prompt corpus
Context-handling test coverage: for top-10 customer prompt shapes, fallback variant truncation rate <= 0.1% relative to primary variant
Tooling parity harness validates function/tool calling signatures for each fallback variant and catches schema/arg serialisation mismatches
Compatibility matrix in Console is updated programmatically from the daily job and shows pass/fail per-variant and per-dimension (tokenizer, context, tools)
Patch or plan created for any variant failing parity tests within 48 hours and a migration/canary mitigation defined
Runbook updated and on-call alerted threshold set (tokenization-mismatch > 1% or tool-call-failures > 0.5%)
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Run daily audit in staging for all fallback variants referenced by SmartRouting policies (no changes to routing) - 2 weeks
Stage 2: Expand audit to prod mirror traffic and feed results to Console compatibility dashboard - 1 week
Stage 3: For variants failing tests, create canary routing rule that prefers next-compatible fallback and enable automatic region/tier steering fallback - gated rollout
Stage 4: After fixes, mark variant as compatible and remove canary overrides in 2-week stabilization window
test_plan: Build tokenizer-diff microservice that takes sample prompts and returns per-token mapping and divergence metrics
Create context-emulation harness that measures effective receptive field and truncation behavior across varying sequence lengths and tokenizers
Function-call smoke tests: instrument 200 synthetic function-calling prompts and verify identical arg/return shapes within tolerance thresholds
Backfill last 30 days of production prompts (anonymized) to compute historical mismatch baselines
Add nightly integration that fails build if any critical variant regresses on regression prompt set
automation: Daily job: tokenizer-diff-runner -> uploads report to S3 and updates compatibility-table service
Alerting: create PagerDuty trigger when mismatch thresholds exceeded
Auto-suppress: routing policy will temporarily avoid an offending fallback for 24h if tool-call failures detected
PR template: add checklist for variant onboarding that includes tokenizer id, vocab hash, max_context, and tooling smoke test results
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives from tokenizer diffs on harmless normalization differences. Mitigation: add normalization-aware comparator and white-list common no-op differences.
Risk: increased nightly job cost and S3 storage. Mitigation: sample intelligently and keep monthly aggregates; expire raw diffs after 30 days.
Risk: over-eager routing avoidance could reduce capacity. Mitigation: prefer next-compatible fallback and use canary percentages rather than global disables.
Risk: variant vendors may not patch quickly. Mitigation: maintain a staged rollback plan and update model catalog with compatibility annotations for sales/CS teams.
